method: Selected normalized GitHub connector comment bodies, retrieved 2026-11-23. These preserve maintainer-reported observations; raw native originals and retained synthesis were not independently acquired by this research.

comments.body:
New accepted-source observations from main `f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5`, [controller job](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45156202495/job/137636936890): 5,031 s job elapsed (83 min 51 s). The authenticated controller JSON is 1,682,588,866 bytes; all 21 original CI ZIPs total 180,364,669 bytes. Checkpoint traces alone retain 1,220,331,199 original bytes across the complete 68-invocation / 69-trace-process workload.

Checkpoint observer statistics: 826.01 s elapsed, 24.51 s CPU, 3,393,593,344-byte lifetime RSS high-water; process-excludes-children, not native command CPU/memory. The original report, raw statistics and independent acceptance are retained. This successful run supplies actual current evidence, superseding no failed evidence.

The accepted report size and controller critical-path cost justify prioritizing attribution of avoidable trace repetition, serialization and repeated decoding/copies before adding more native workloads. Preserve actual installed import/custody/process/syscall observations, complete counterexamples and original-evidence independence. This remains non-contractual profiling work: no numerical timing/memory gate, list cap, approval-to-proceed condition or inferred OOM diagnosis is introduced.

Offline attribution of accepted originals is complete for main `f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5`. Actual Actions step timings put **4,976 s (82 min 56 s)** in native enrollment and **32 s** in artifact upload; the full controller job was 5,031 s. The large report therefore does not by itself explain the elapsed time as upload overhead. Checkpoint qualification accounts for 826.01 s (13 min 46 s). Its 68 invocation clocks sum to 542.05 s, but held-process/concurrent counterexample clocks can overlap; this sum is not subtracted as an exclusive overhead measurement. These different measurement scopes must not be combined as independent totals.

One complete descriptive fd/path-attribution pass over all 69 original checkpoint traces assigns 1,142,250,033 of 1,220,331,199 trace-text bytes (93.6%) to read calls on installed runtime/package/schema files. Checkpoint authority-file read lines account for 56,266 bytes. Repeated installed-module/schema reads are visible across all 69 trace processes. The attribution parser has an invented descriptor-reuse/aligned-close control, authenticates every original trace, and changes no qualification. It does not establish a causal timing saving by itself.

The next conservative experiment is to evaluate avoiding excessive rendering/repeated copies of unrelated import data while retaining every original syscall/process/custody counterexample and exact required record/marker/request/reply byte proof. Any rendering adjustment must continue to reject truncated required evidence. Keep the 68-invocation/69-trace-process workload and all inherited qualification scopes unchanged. Native capture/restore phases also remain profiling candidates; nested phase statistics overlap and are not additive.

Retained attribution SHA-256: `eea8e1ded7087e6a2738490971719780826d5c9efecab870cc19cf0c746d6bf6`. Its own descriptive scan took 16.29 s and executed no native payload. This remains an advisory implementation/performance investigation, with no new timing gate or approval condition.

Qualification cost and scaling review on accepted main `f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5`. Product implementation is paused at the maintainer's explicit request; #450 has not started. This review changes no source, gates, workload, growth bound or qualification claim.

**Recommendation: keep the proof obligations, but change the qualification structure before extending the serial native workload.** The present accumulation of fixtures, shared images and whole-report readers is a poor default for the complete implementation plan. The evidence does not establish that native qualification itself is infeasible or that normal product performance is poor. Maximal test speed is not the objective; predictable growth in total work, retained evidence and feedback time is.

### What the 84 minutes contain

The [accepted controller job](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45156202495/job/137636936890) took **83m51s**. The actual enrollment Actions step took 82m56s and artifact upload 32s. Nested timers were reconciled by subtracting direct-child durations, with a hand-computed nesting control. The following groups are mutually exclusive and sum to 82m49s of instrumented native stages, rather than double-counting capture, restore and restored boot:

| Measured native work | Elapsed | Share of instrumented stages |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Disk-copy stages across the two owned restore paths | 16m33s | 20.0% |
| Installed protected entrypoint checks | 14m11s | 17.1% |
| Protected checkpoint checks | 13m00s | 15.7% |
| Readiness of the three guest sessions | 6m25s | 7.7% |
| All other native stages | 32m41s | 39.5% |

The broader checkpoint observer lifetime was 13m46s; it includes work outside the named 13-minute stage. Its invocation clocks overlap and are not additional serial time. The previously reported 23-minute capture lifetime contains restore and restored-boot work; it is not 23 minutes of standalone snapshot copying.

[Main CI](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45156202495) took **101m06s**, including queues and dependencies, and used **276.6 summed runner-minutes**. The longest unit job was 34m26s; its actual pytest scope was 32m57s. [PR CI](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45148737751) took 44m18s and 199.0 runner-minutes. Adding their separate CodeQL runs gives **482.6 runner-minutes, or 8h03m**, for this successful PR/main cycle. That sum measures occupied job time across concurrent machines, not CPU time, billed minutes or a single 8-hour wait. The two workflow waits sum to 2h25m24s, excluding human review and independent acceptance. Four additionally inspected failed attempts consumed another 15h27m of summed job time; that is a separate retry sample, not a complete campaign total.

### Growth already visible, and its limits

| Accepted main run | Native job | Prerequisite scopes | Standalone root image file | Original aggregate JSON |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [44900090812](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/44900090812) | 45m04s | 34 | 3.49 GB | 5.22 MB |
| [44949812264](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/44949812264) | 54m43s | 35 | 4.51 GB | 26.97 MB |
| [45001739840](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45001739840) | 64m15s | 36 | 4.52 GB | 45.62 MB |
| [45050151755](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45050151755) | 60m02s | 36 | 4.04 GB | 45.62 MB |
| [45156202495](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/actions/runs/45156202495) | 83m51s | 37 | 5.36 GB | 1,682.59 MB |

Sizes use decimal units and describe qcow2 file length, not physical host allocation. Workloads and runner conditions differ. Another accepted 36-scope run took 79m34s, so fitting a timing curve or asserting an empirical quadratic regression would be unjustified. Scope counts are not equivalent features and cannot be used to multiply out a full-product ETA. The current 37 scopes are still prerequisites, while #137 routes a much larger complete implementation across owners, supplied adapters and native profiles.

### Structural amplifiers to address

1. **Fresh processes repeatedly import the entire installed contract collection.** The [validator](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/blob/f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5/packages/fishhat-contracts/src/fishhat_contracts/validation.py#L253) eagerly reads 73 schemas plus 8 catalogues, totaling about 2.04 MB. The checkpoint workload has 68 invocations and 69 traced processes. The authenticated original traces contain **1.22 GB** of text; **93.6%** is read-call text on installed runtime/package/schema files. This is a structural `process count × imported closure extent` cost. It is relevant to cold product commands too, although tracing and software emulation prevent using these times as normal command-latency measurements.

2. **Evidence scratch can enlarge later disk work.** Checkpoint traces are written under the same guest root that is later snapshotted. The writable root image grew by 1.323 GB and the standalone copy by 1.317 GB versus the previous accepted run. Trace files are subsequently unlinked, but there is no intervening discard/compaction boundary in this path. Their size and placement strongly suggest coupling to the 1.22 GB trace workload; this is an inference, not a controlled causal measurement. Later restore work increased from 12m18s to 16m33s while the root copy grew 32.6%. Runner variance prevents attributing that exact time delta to the extra bytes.

3. **Custody helpers repeatedly scan entire disk and evidence closures.** [Copy verification](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/blob/f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5/scripts/native_linux_snapshots.py#L246) calls its verification callback around individual image operations. [Capture lifetime verification](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/blob/f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5/scripts/native_linux_successor.py#L96) hashes the sealed disks and base inputs, compares previously accumulated report evidence, and re-observes the original source. The cost is `verification count × closure byte extent`. It remains linear in disk extent when the verification count is fixed; the concern is allowing both axes to grow as unrelated proof domains accumulate.

4. **Independent acceptance repeats whole-report decoding.** Multiple frozen readers independently consume the same aggregate JSON or ZIP. The 18 inherited reader dispatches took 3m29s in this run, excluding the new checkpoint reader and final acceptance, so they do not explain the 84-minute CI job. Their growth still matters: `whole-report reader count × aggregate evidence extent` can become quadratic in added proof domains if both grow together. One existing data-only scan reached about 3.4 GB lifetime RSS. That is process-scoped memory, not simultaneous guest/host memory, and does not diagnose an OOM.

These are structural models, not measured whole-pipeline forecasts. Doubling both axes in any one multiplication makes that subset's work fourfold. Improving VM speed would reduce constants without removing these couplings. The [current guest](https://github.com/nashspence/fishhat/blob/f96b83dc20f059d62a4363a63c37bb0ef8c642e5/scripts/native_linux_guest.py#L352) uses TCG software emulation, not KVM.

### Recommended sequence, with proof-preservation checks

1. **Separate observation evidence from the state image being qualified.** Use an explicitly owned ephemeral evidence sink/volume or authenticated stream, with independently verified identity, original bytes, process joins and cleanup. First run a matched old/new experiment on the same complete 68-invocation/69-process workload. Record bytes written into each image, source/copy sizes, elapsed/CPU/I/O and unchanged success, tamper, interruption and cleanup outcomes. Do not solve this by truncating traces, capping evidence or moving it into a protected authority/journal domain.

2. **Give each proof scope its own original evidence closure.** Retain full required originals separately from compact outcomes, with an authenticated index binding exact source, run, attempt, installed artifacts, native profile and all required scopes. Independent readers should validate their own closure; the aggregate must still reject missing/duplicate scopes, cross-run substitutions, truncation and producer-invented success. Stream large originals rather than repeatedly embedding/copying them through one giant JSON value. This reduces cross-feature amplification while preserving independence from producer validators.

3. **Measure and redesign repeated full-closure verification.** Add work observations for hash bytes, file reads and custody transitions, then identify equivalent verification boundaries. Any consolidation must retain all mutation/rebinding/alias/permission checks and fail the same adversarial controls. A remembered digest or unchanged metadata alone is not an adequate substitute for protected immutable custody. No full scan is removed merely because it is expensive.

4. **Partition native work by independently owned fixture lifetime and proof domain.** Run suitable scopes in separate enrolled disposable guests/jobs and reconcile their complete current-run receipts. Preserve sequential work where a promise actually spans a reboot, restore, authority handoff or failure lifetime. Share only independently verified immutable inputs; do not share writable authority or a live guest between competing jobs. All present required scopes remain required on main. Size the useful parallel lanes around the longest necessary lane, including unit work, rather than forcing every job below an arbitrary short duration. Parallelism shortens feedback but does not, by itself, reduce total runner work.

5. **Then profile the recurring unit and cold-import costs.** Current unit cases still spend roughly 12–19 minutes individually in aggregate-growth/negative-control workloads, overlapping under four-worker xdist. Their meters use Python tracing, complete semantic validation and real counted work. Profile the instrumentation and implementation separately, retain every input extent and injected superlinear regression, and demonstrate equivalent coverage before changing how counting works. More shards cannot shorten an indivisible case. Evaluate lazy, closed-reference-safe schema loading separately; preserve complete validation and independent installed-artifact custody rather than avoiding process-isolation witnesses.

Keep the finite-profile plan: qualify claimed compositions and each routed adapter/owner obligation, with cross-owner end-to-end cases where the promise spans owners. Do not grow an unconditional Cartesian product of every unrelated implementation, state scale and failure position. This is not permission to remove an existing required case or to leave a promised composition unqualified.

GitHub currently documents a [six-hour hosted-job ceiling](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits) and [4-CPU/16-GB standard public Ubuntu runners](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners). Those ceilings are not desirable feedback targets. Retaining one ever-growing serial qualification job is likely to become impractical before reaching them; adding workers without controlling total evidence/scan growth would merely spend more capacity.

No required proof is being moved to an optional nightly lane, no fresh-main/source policy is being waived, and no new numerical performance gate is proposed. Normal product performance should later be measured through representative maintained commands, cold/warm starts and growing histories outside heavy tracing, while retaining separate correctness, extent and required linear-work proofs. This review cannot establish a comparison with competing products before real product operations exist.

The offline review authenticated **23 original workflow runs**, including 16 accepted main milestones and four failed attempts; **20 controller logs** were reconciled. No new CI/native workload was executed. Retained synthesis SHA-256: `9d714189fdd2b1ca45b6432f1448e3bb7cdbf83094574bce1f9f48fbe14ae79a`. The earlier complete trace attribution and accepted source/evidence identities remain in the preceding comments. Product work remains paused for the maintainer's review of this accounting and recommended sequence.
